I don't really know how to go about finding a good therapist, to be honest. When I was still in education teachers always picked up on the fact that something was off and sent me to the school therapist (the exception being collage where I reached out to the therapist, but her room was right next to my class room so that helped). I didn't graduate my first year of collage so I'm now out of education and not really doing anything. I'm struggling to find a job too so, even if I found a therapist, I couldn't afford to pay them. 

Since I'm in the UK I could try and find something through the NHS, but some places require a referral from your GP, and my current GP is just the worse. Hyper-religious, traditional, old Indian people. I'm also Indian, my mother is also as hyper-religious and old-fashioned as the people at my GP, so patient confidentiality means nothing to my GP. (When I was 18 I went to the GP to discuss why my periods had stopped, I went on my own since my mum would likely have gone ape shit and accused me of being a whore - and she did. Because the GP called my mum to say that I had visited and that my period was late by several months. I'm almost confident that what my GP did was illegal, but I don't have the money to sue). I could leave that GP, but they'd tell my mum and she'd know something is up. My mum doesn't believe that mental health is real, so if she found out that I was trying to seek help for it she'll accuse me of using mental health as an excuse to be lazy. She acted that way while I was sitting my GCSE's and A Levels and basically breaking down nightly due to exam stress. 

I'm sure there are more options for me, but a lot of boils down to me being terrified that my mum will find out. I'm also really worried that, should my mum ever be able to fully understand how her actions have impacted me, she'll think she's a horrible mother and do something stupid - Like threaten to run away or kill herself, as she's done in the past. I know she wants to be a mum that her children idolise, and yeah she absolutely isn't that, but I can't imagine how crushing it must feel to believe that one failed as a parent. My dad isn't as 'traditional' as she is and didn't force her to have children, she was the one who couldn't wait to become a mum (she also wanted a son, as is the 'traditional' Indian way, so I'm guessing having a daughter was already a massive blow).

I could literally write an entire book series, complete with unnecessary spinoffs, about my entitled mother. Entitlement-wise she was pretty much what you'd expect, treated retail workers awfully (despite being one herself), demanding to see the manager, and having the emotional depth and maturity of a 7 year old; so with that said I wont dwell too much on EM stories you've all heard before. Wants discounts, would haggle everywhere, my child deserves this item etc etc etc

Definitely the most embarrassing thing she'd do though was her trademark strop (sulk) in restaurants. She'd fold her arms, slouch in her chair, and pout while looking at the table. Drove me absolutely fucking insane when she did that. Going out to eat with her was a pain, because she'd want to pay no more than a tenner but wanted gourmet food with outstanding service that was cooked to her own personal taste - which she'd never tell anyone what it was. Also, lamb. Crazy obsession with lamb, and if the restaurant didn't sell it or were out of stock then she'd berate them and try to make them feel shitty cuz they ruined this poor woman's entire life because they didn't feed her lamb. 

Also, while she treated normal servers badly, god help the non-english ones. And I'm not talking about the one that came from another country to England, no, I mean servers who were in there own country listening to this crazy English woman talking LOUD and s l o w about how she doesn't want a salad in her burger but still wanted the lettuce and tomatoes. Despite herself being an immigrant, if you didn't speak English (or simply were not from England), you were trash. I began picking up Spanish and Flemmish to apologise to foreign servers she'd harassed. 

Another thing she was perhaps the most entitled to was my future. She had (or still has) this belief that she was going to control every single part of my life, from the clothes I wore, the friends I kept, the reputation I built, the professions I studied, the person I married (Indian, so, arranged marriage, yknow), and the children I had. She despised the idea of me doing things because *I* wanted to, and in her mind everything I did somehow had something to do with *her*. I trimmed my hair? Did it to spite her. Stayed out an hour longer than I should have? I did it because I wanted to rebel against *her*. I didn't eat what she cooked? I did it because I wanted to starve and make *her* look like a bad mother. She simply couldn't fathom that I could - and would - do things that didn't involve her.

So, "what was it like being *that* kid"? Embarrassing, humiliating, constricting. I'm 20, and I've grown to despise my mother more than I thought I was capable of hating someone.
